question_text: How do you distinguish a male frog from a female frog?

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Vocal sacs
steps.margin_note: Name the character, its position and its use. Two characters, one mark each.
lines: A male frog carries secondary sexual
characters. They are absent in the female frog.
1) The male has a pair of vocal sacs at the
They swell with air and make the croak louder.
steps.why: Both differences are secondary sexual characters of the male, so the answer is written as two things the male has and the female lacks.
common_mistakes: Describing the female instead. The female has neither character; write what the male has.
Placing the vocal sacs on the throat middle. They lie at the angles of the lower jaw.
steps.memory_tip: Two male marks: sacs at the jaw for sound, pad on the thumb for holding.

steps.label: Copulatory pad
steps.margin_note: One boxed line names both male characters; the rest gives position and use.

lines.text: Male frog: vocal sacs + copulatory pad

lines: 2) The male has a copulatory pad on the first
It helps him hold the female during mating.
The female frog has neither of these, and her
steps.why: The copulatory pad holds the female, so it sits on the digit that presses against her body during mating, and it appears only in the male.
common_mistakes: Calling it a nuptial pad on the hind limb. It is on the first digit of the FORElimb.
Writing that both sexes have the pad. Only the male has it.
steps.memory_tip: First digit of the front limb: the thumb pad that holds the female.

insider_note: Both marks are for the male's two characters; a line saying the female is bigger is true but earns nothing on its own.
